summary_markdown:
The conversation focused on analyzing an unexplained, sharp peak in device session data recorded at a specific time (14:22–14:24 local time) on September 22nd. Initial analysis of the raw and grouped session concepts showed that the traffic pattern appeared normal, suggesting no anomalous spammer activity.

Discussion points included:
*   The two physical data boxes are located near a road, not in the same building.
*   It was confirmed that the MAC address salt used on both boxes is identical, indicating they captured data from two distinct groups of people who were close to each other but separate.
*   Given the lack of comparative data (only one full day's worth), it was suggested that the best course of action is to directly ask local personnel what activity occurred during the observed time window. If no major event took place, the spike can be attributed to normal test operation or calibration activities.
decisions: The unusual session data spike will be addressed by asking local staff about potential events that occurred at 14:22–14:24 on September 22nd.
action_items: Someone needs to pass the findings and questions regarding the data spike to Andrii Vasilchenko.
